svg.title: Get the installers without buying cloud resources — instructional mockup
svg.desc: Step-specific guided recreation. Not a genuine screenshot or live result.
svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Get the installers without buying cloud resources
Your Windows 10 host · Windows PowerShell
Windows PowerShell — Windows host
COMMAND / FILE CONTENT TO ENTER — PRESERVE CASE
Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 "$env:USERPROFILE\Downloads\rhel-9.x-x86_64-dvd.iso"
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
A SHA256 row appears. Its hash must exactly match Red Hat’s checksum for your exact ISO; the
version in your filename may differ.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. Open a browser on Windows. Visit the official Red Hat Developer RHEL page linked below and sign in or
create your own account.
2. Review the current Developer subscription terms, then choose the RHEL 9 x86_64 DVD ISO. Do not choose
RHEL 10 or an ARM image.
3. Save the ISO in Downloads. Use Red Hat’s published checksum and the command below; replace the
example filename with the filename you downloaded.
4. If VMware Workstation Pro is not installed, follow the academy’s existing VMware setup lesson linked
in the course resources, using the official Broadcom download. Install it on Windows and reopen it.
5. If you want a graphical browser check later, install a current Firefox on Windows from Mozilla. We
will use a separate practice profile.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
